name: FFL Monkey Checkout for WooCommerce
author: FFLMonkey.com

sections.description:
In the United States a firearm bought online is not shipped to the buyer. It
ships to a federally licensed dealer, an FFL, who completes the transfer in
person. This plugin adds that step to a WooCommerce checkout.

What it does

  • Adds a dealer picker to checkout, in both the Checkout block and the classic
    checkout. The buyer searches by ZIP code, or by their location if they
    choose to share it, and picks a dealer from a list and a map.
  • Shows what is listed about each dealer: reviews, kind of business, services,
    hours, listed transfer fees, and links to the dealer’s website, Google and
    social pages. Listed fees are marked as not confirmed.
  • Splits a mixed cart. Items that need a dealer ship to the dealer; everything
    else ships to the buyer’s own address, as a separate package.
  • Holds the order until the requirement is met. A dealer whose licence has
    expired is refused, and an order with an NFA item needs a dealer with a
    Special Occupational Tax (SOT) on record.
  • Records the chosen dealer on the order and shows it on the order screen, with
    a link to the ATF’s FFL eZ Check.
  • Optionally lets buyers collect from your own premises, upload a licence for a
    dealer that is not listed, or place the order now and name a dealer later.
  • Adds a checkbox to each product for “ships to a dealer”, and one for NFA
    items that need an SOT dealer.

Requires an account

The dealer directory the picker searches is a service run by FFLMonkey.com, a
paid subscription. The plugin cannot search for dealers without an account at
https://fflmonkey.com, which the setup screen creates or signs in to.

The plugin itself is free software under the GPL and contains no locked,
time-limited or paid-only code. A subscription buys access to the service’s
dealer directory, not to features of this plugin.

Requirements

  • WooCommerce
  • PHP 7.2 or newer
  • An account at FFLMonkey.com

External services

The plugin uses five external services. None is contacted until you choose
Create an account or I already have an account on the plugin’s page (or, if
the FFL Monkey Data Feed plugin is connected on this store, until you open the
page), or press an eZ Check control on an order (4, below).
Activating or deactivating the plugin sends nothing. Once the store is connected, the transfer of each
order that needs a dealer is sent to FFLMonkey.com, and it includes the
buyer’s name, email address, phone number and addresses (below). Nothing about
buyers is sent to OpenFreeMap or OpenStreetMap.

1. FFLMonkey.com, https://backend.fflmonkey.com

Runs the dealer directory and your account.

  • Setup, from your server, while the store is not connected: when you choose
    Create an account or I already have an account, a request for the sign-in
    choices on offer, which says nothing about your store. When you sign in, your
    email and password; when you create an account, your name, email and
    password, and your business name and how you found FFL Monkey if you give
    them. With either, your site’s address and name, your admin URL and an
    identifier for this installation; during setup, the licence and plan you
    choose. If the FFL Monkey Data Feed plugin is connected on this store, its
    licence key is sent when you open the page, so you are signed in without
    typing your password. Choosing a paid plan opens Stripe’s checkout in a new
    tab.
  • Admin screens, once the store is connected: your site and admin URLs, the
    licence key the plugin holds and the product name.
  • The Dealer licences and Account tabs, from your browser, once the store is
    connected: these tabs load the dealer licences and SOT stamps you uploaded
    there, and your subscription, directly from this host, using a short-lived
    token the plugin obtains for them. The licence and stamp files you drop or
    choose on the Dealer licences tab are sent to this host, which reads them
    to find each dealer. As with any web request, the browser also sends its IP
    address. Subscribing or managing billing opens a new tab on this host, which
    passes you to Stripe to pay.
  • Dealer search, from the buyer’s browser: the ZIP code searched (or the
    buyer’s coordinates, only if they choose “Use my location”), the store’s
    public dealer-search key and, if the buyer uploads a dealer’s licence, that
    file. As with any web request, the browser also sends its IP address. A
    dealer’s panel can link to the dealer’s own website and to its Google,
    Facebook, Instagram, Yelp, X and LinkedIn pages, each opening in a new tab
    only when the buyer clicks it.
  • At checkout, from your server: the chosen dealer’s licence number, to check
    it is valid.
  • At checkout, for a connected store whose cart holds products Data Feed
    brought in and ships to a US state, from your server: those products’
    catalog IDs and the state, with the store’s licence ID and API token, to ask
    which of them that state’s law restricts. The answer is kept for 15 minutes.
  • When a dealer is recorded on an order after checkout, from your server: that
    dealer’s licence number, to fetch their name, address, licence expiry and
    contact details. This happens whatever the dealer verification setting,
    for an FFL number you type or pick in the order’s FFL transfer box, a dealer
    the buyer chooses from the link in their email, and the dealer of an
    approved upload.
  • Every 15 minutes, for a connected store with orders waiting on a dealer
    licence the buyer uploaded, from your server: each upload’s reference, with
    the store’s licence ID and API token, to ask whether FFLMonkey.com has read
    and approved it, and for the dealer’s licence number once it has.
  • When an order is placed and completed: a reference for the order, made from
    its order key so that the key itself is never sent, the dealer’s licence
    number, name, address and licence expiry, and whether a dealer was named.
  • The FFL transfer of each order that needs a dealer, for a connected store,
    whenever it changes: its code, status and history (who did what, and when),
    the order’s number, status, currency and total, the buyer’s name, email
    address, phone number and billing and shipping addresses, the items ordered,
    the dealer’s details, contact and answer, and the carrier, tracking number
    and serial numbers once you mark it shipped.
  • When a transfer request is emailed to a dealer, from your server: your FFL
    number, to fetch the copy of your FFL (and SOT, for an NFA order) that
    FFLMonkey.com holds, to attach it.
  • When a dealer sends their FFL or SOT copy from their answer page, from your
    server: that file, with the store’s public dealer-search key.
  • When the store’s licence has stopped (a failed payment, an ended trial or
    free period, a cancelled subscription) and you open the plugin’s page, from
    your server: the store’s licence ID and API token, to ask whether a
    subscription restores it; and when you choose a plan, that plan, to open
    Stripe’s checkout (5, below).
  • When you download a dealer’s FFL or SOT copy from an order, from your
    server: that dealer’s licence number, with the store’s API token.
  • Your own FFL or SOT document, if you upload one on the Your FFL tab: from
    your browser, with the store’s short-lived sign-in for its FFL Monkey
    screens, or from your server when the page cannot send it directly.
  • Support tickets, for a connected store: what you write and any files you
    attach, from your browser, with the name and email of the WordPress user who
    sends it, your site’s address, and your plugin, WordPress, WooCommerce and
    PHP versions. Never your licence key or any password. While you are in
    wp-admin, your server also asks whether a reply is waiting for you, at most
    once a minute, with the store’s licence ID and API token.

Terms: https://fflmonkey.com/legal/terms
Privacy: https://fflmonkey.com/legal/privacy

2. OpenFreeMap, https://tiles.openfreemap.org

The picker’s map is drawn from OpenFreeMap’s map style, tiles and fonts,
loaded by the buyer’s browser when results are shown. Each request carries the
buyer’s IP address and the referrer your site’s policy allows (by default your
store’s origin, never the page address).

Terms: https://openfreemap.org/tos/
Privacy: https://openfreemap.org/privacy/

3. OpenStreetMap, https://tile.openstreetmap.org

When OpenFreeMap’s map cannot be drawn (it does not load, or the buyer’s
browser has no WebGL), the picker’s map is drawn from OpenStreetMap tiles
instead, loaded by the buyer’s browser. Each request carries the buyer’s IP
address and your store’s origin as the referrer (never the page address),
which the tile policy requires.

Terms: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Terms_of_Use
Privacy: https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy

4. ATF FFL eZ Check, https://fflezcheck.atf.gov

The public licence lookup of the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and
Explosives. When you press “ATF eZ Check” or “Verify on ATF eZ Check” in an
order’s FFL transfer box, your browser opens eZ Check in a new tab and posts
the dealer’s licence number to its search (the region, district and last five
digits, the fields the search asks for), to show whether the licence is
current. Nothing is sent until you press it, and nothing about the buyer is
sent. As with any web request, the browser also sends its IP address.

Terms: the system use notice on https://fflezcheck.atf.gov/FFLEzCheck/
Privacy: https://www.justice.gov/doj/privacy-policy

5. Stripe Checkout, https://checkout.stripe.com

Choosing a paid plan during setup, or on the plugin’s page once the store’s
licence has stopped, opens Stripe’s checkout in a new tab, where you pay. FFLMonkey.com creates the
checkout; the plugin sends nothing to Stripe itself, and your card details
never touch your site.

Terms: https://stripe.com/legal
Privacy: https://stripe.com/privacy

Credits

The merchant screens bundled in this plugin show department icons from Game
Icons (https://game-icons.net), by Lorc, Delapouite and contributors, licensed
under CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/).
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Install and activate this plugin.
  3. Open FFLMonkey.com → Checkout in the admin menu and follow the setup
    steps. You sign in or create an account inside the panel and the store
    connects itself. Nothing has to be copied or pasted.
  4. On each product that must ship to a dealer, tick the box on its edit screen.
  5. Review the Your FFL and Appearance tabs.
sections.faq:
Do I need an account?

Yes. The dealer directory is a service run by FFLMonkey.com, and the plugin
needs an account there to search it.

Does it work with the Checkout block?

Yes. The same picker appears in the Checkout block and in the classic
checkout, and both enforce the same rules.

What happens to a cart with a firearm and a holster?

It is split into two packages. The firearm ships to the chosen dealer and the
holster ships to the buyer, each with its own shipping options.

What if the buyer’s dealer is not in the directory?

The buyer can upload the dealer’s licence, or place the order and name a
dealer later. You can also let buyers collect from your own premises on the
Your FFL tab.

Is the source code available?

Yes. The plugin is licensed GPLv2 or later and its full source is in the
download. The PHP is in src/. The browser scripts in assets/dist/ are
compiled; their source is in assets/src/ and, for the dealer picker,
source/checkout-sdk/, with the build configuration at the plugin root. The
licences of the libraries bundled into the picker are in source/licenses/.
sections.changelog:
1.8.0

  • After setup, FFL Checkout says what is true of your website: with no product marked it says how to mark one, and a tour walks the tabs the first time.
  • Support says when to expect an answer and updates by itself, and a solved ticket stays solved until you reopen it. Buttons explain themselves in a tooltip.
  • Every file in the zip says GPLv2 or later.

1.7.0

  • A dealer in the search shows its reviews, kind of business, services, hours and links to its website, Google and social pages, and its listed transfer fees, marked as not confirmed.

1.6.1

  • The new FFL Monkey logo on the Checkout, setup and Support pages, three orange stripes in the menu, and a new banner and icon on the plugin’s WordPress.org page.

1.6.0

  • The dealer’s page has a new look, laid out like the FFL Monkey account, and a dealer answering from a page left open is told the transfer was already answered.

1.5.0

  • The full-screen dealer search keeps keyboard focus inside it, and a dealer row’s grey lines are easier to read.
  • Transfers and Dealer licences read on a phone or tablet.
  • The dealer’s answer page keeps what the dealer typed when an answer is refused.
  • The FFL transfer box says when a dealer’s copy is not on file yet, and asks for a missing dealer email.
  • The plan step says who the free days are for, a buyer reads each checkout error once, and a reference code shows only when something failed on our side.

1.4.0

  • Setup: the first screen asks FFL Monkey nothing until you choose to create an account or sign in. The first connect opens a short setup (your FFL licence, store pickup, the picker’s wording and colour), then Transfers.
  • Your FFL: your licence goes straight to FFL Monkey from your browser, up to 10 MB, so your host’s upload limit no longer refuses a phone photo. Your shop’s phone is checked as a phone number.
  • Transfers: a transfer’s buttons open the order at its FFL transfer box, and recording a dealer’s answer by phone starts with no answer chosen.
  • Account: a cancelled plan is kept in one click, and support’s details sit under a closed Details for support.
  • A store that ships nothing is told so, and its orders still name the dealer. A connection FFL Monkey refuses is said once, with Reconnect.
  • The page shows the plugin’s version and whether it is the newest.

1.3.1

  • Transfers: the dealer a buyer picks from the link in their email is read from a cleaned copy of the form. Nothing you or buyers see changes.

1.3.0

  • Setup: creating an account, signing in and choosing a plan happen on the FFL Checkout page itself, then the page opens on Your FFL. A store running FFL Monkey Data Feed is signed in as the page opens.
  • Settings: leaving Your FFL or Appearance with changes not saved asks first.

1.2.0

  • Ammunition shipped to California goes to a dealer: the dealer picker appears for it, the buyer ticks that their dealer is a California licensed ammunition vendor, and the ammunition goes in the dealer’s parcel and on the dealer’s request. Elsewhere it ships to the buyer as before.

1.1.0

  • FFL transfers: every firearm order opens a transfer. The dealer is asked by email and answers on your store, and you follow it from a Transfers tab, an FFL transfer box on the order and a printable record. The buyer gets an email at each step.
  • Dealer picker: the dealer’s details in two numbered steps with Directions and Call, an uploaded licence read while the buyer waits, and the picker can sit inside the Checkout block.
  • Your FFL tab (formerly Collection) and Dealer licences tab for your own licence, SOT stamp and the licences you collect.
  • Appearance: a colour window for the picker’s colour, and the Search button text now changes the search button.
  • Setup and billing: the payment wait and the payment and licence pages share one clear card, and every error ends with a reference to quote.
  • Account: a licence that works without a plan says Free access and offers no plan.
  • Your FFL: a chosen file shows it is sending, the tab follows the check without a reload, and Send a different file opens the upload with a Back button.
  • Missing values read “None” instead of a dash.

1.0.0

  • First public release.
  • Dealer picker for the Checkout block and the classic checkout, with ZIP and
    location search, a list and a map.
  • Splits carts between the dealer and the buyer, and holds orders until the
    dealer requirement is met.
  • The map shows on stores that send a strict referrer policy.
